sections.what: Avenue 360 provides primary, dental, behavioral and HIV healthcare across Houston-area clinics. Its HIV services combine rapid treatment linkage, medication support, PrEP and case management. Housing assistance and supportive services seek to reduce barriers to continuing care and stable daily life.
sections.monitoring: Original 2023 reports 13,232 unduplicated healthcare individuals and 41,870 visits, plus housing assistance for 521 clients and others in their households. These groups may overlap and are not added. Current 2024 return describes HIV/intensive case management and CoC/HOPWA housing but no recovered numerical current housing cohort. Request current distinct households, additional stable housing, ART retention, utility follow-up and actual payment/disruption incidence. Public housing and insurance alternatives are baseline.
sections.qualitative: Original returns distinguish the healthcare recipient from a related zero-expense affiliate. HIV treatment, housing and transportation barriers provide concrete connected mechanisms. Historical original housing payments identify a resource channel rather than merely retail medical value. Current unique housing and completed HIV treatment cohorts are not verified. Clinical utility and additional net housing resources are unsupported local priors. Public housing grants, insurance and other HIV providers complicate additionality and marginal funding. Original HACS EIN 76-0549240 doing business as Avenue 360 matches the historical recipient-owned 990. BeringOmega EIN 76-0589592 is a related recipient, not zero cost for this clinical operation. Donation route checked, not transaction/payee restrictions.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $231.36 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 0.982612 clinical QALYs and 0.482176 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.000432 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $33,889,527. Historical 521 housing clients are a reference proxy, not current independent households: judged .8 mapping ×.25 additional annual implementation. Clinical .25 improvement ×.04 utility ×1 finite year is a weak HIV-care/housing morbidity hypothesis, not ART trial calibration, PrEP infection-count conversion or mortality credit. Independent .5 resource success with $1,000 net additional housing resources after tax/benefit offsets and alternative assistance uses positive overlap .5 minus full $100 one-off application, move, travel or foregone-pay burden. Successful households net $400; others lose $100. Union 104.2 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 26.05; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $15,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Housing payments are transfers, not new production. Full matched counterparty incidence is stressed separately; annual grants already included in recipient cost are not charged a second time as identical provider expense. Separate taxpayer/displaced-beneficiary loss applies only to truly additional budget/displacement, unknown centrally. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY 2024 recognized tax expense $33,889,527;FY 2023$34,952,120;FY 2022$40,128,430. No populated event/rental/inventory addback recovered, and current ScheduleD expenses removed 0; unrecognized volunteers or partner resources are not provenzero. FY 2023 housing payments $4,608,711 for 521 clients/othersHH are historical gross transfers, not net current consumption gain. Current whole-recipient cost and historical proxy mismatch is explicit. Other clinical, prevention, hospice and housing outcomes remain unknown.

model.costScope: Whole healthcare recipient recognized annual expense versus limited historical housing/HIV-care channel; partner resources and marginal gift unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Houston-area delivery; .95 local household share judged, not measured residence
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: CoC/HOPWA and other public housing, Medicaid/insurance, RyanWhite/other HIV providers and family support remain baseline
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional stable occupied housing and continued appropriate HIV care in a reference household cohort; payments and visits not QALYs
